newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: No problems with Yeltsin control, premier says.
newsitem.headline: No problems with Yeltsin control, premier says.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin is fully capable of coping with all the affairs of state, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Thursday.
But he also told a news conference in this Swiss mountain resort that it "takes time to get over pneumonia" and said best wishes should be sent to Yeltsin for a quick recovery.
Asked if the ailing Kremlin chief was able to handle state affairs while his prime minister was out of the country, Chernomyrdin replied: "Yes, he can and he is doing it."
He added: "If there had been any doubt, and if there had been any problem, I would not have come to Davos."

Chernomyrdin, attending the annual World Economic Forum, said on return to Moscow on Saturday, Yeltsin's birthday, he would go straight to see the President and congratulate him, "with a bouquet of flowers and a gift."

"Let us all wish him a speedy recovery.... Anyone takes time to get over pneumonia," he added. He said Yeltsin, who was in the Kremlin earlier on Thursday, would meet President Jacques Chirac of France next week and U.S. President Bill Clinton in Moscow as scheduled in March.
